Definition: Mehetabel, the name of an Edomitish man and woman
BiblicalUsage: Mehetabel is the name of two people: the wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom, and the daughter of Matred. A second Mehetabel is the father of Shemaiah, who tried to frighten Nehemiah into hiding in the temple.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the two Mehetabels show how a name travels: one is a king's wife in Edom, the other a father in Jerusalem, and the same name covers a queen and a plotter — the Bible keeps both.
